subject: computer
question: Which of these is an input device?
explanation: A keyboard sends data into the computer; printers, speakers and monitors are output devices.

subject: computer
question: Which memory loses its contents when the power is switched off?
explanation: RAM is volatile memory: it needs power to keep data.

subject: computer
question: Which part of a computer is called its 'brain'?
explanation: The CPU (Central Processing Unit) carries out instructions, so it is called the brain of the computer.

subject: computer
question: Which small, fast memory sits between the CPU and main memory to speed up access?
explanation: Cache memory keeps frequently used data close to the CPU.

subject: computer
question: The program that starts the computer and checks the hardware when it is switched on is stored in:
explanation: The BIOS/UEFI firmware is stored in non-volatile ROM so it is available at start-up.

subject: computer
question: Which part of the CPU performs arithmetic and logical operations?
explanation: The ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit) does calculations and comparisons; the control unit directs the work.
